title: Palm Sunday and Holy Week
hookLine: branches in, a cross by Friday; the week the whole year turns on

lines: BRANCHES AND CLOAKS ON THE ROAD.
cards: Jerusalem, a few days before Passover. The city is packed with pilgrims, and Roman soldiers are watching the crowds. A man comes over the Mount of Olives riding a young donkey.
Not a warhorse. A donkey. And the crowd goes wild.
People throw their cloaks on the road in front of him. Others cut branches from the trees.
John's Gospel says they "Took branches of palm trees, and went forth to meet him, and cried, Hosanna: Blessed is the King of Israel that cometh in the name of the Lord."

teach.b: Start with the shout. Hosanna sounds like praise, and became praise, but began as a plea, from Hebrew in Psalm 118: save, please. Save us now.
The crowd is shouting praise and a prayer for rescue at once. And the donkey matters.
The prophet Zechariah had pictured Jerusalem's king coming humble, riding on a donkey. Jesus seems to choose that picture on purpose: a king, but not the kind with an army.
In the Gospels, Jesus clears the traders out of the temple. He teaches in its courts. A woman anoints him with costly perfume.
On Thursday, a last supper with his friends. On Friday, the cross. On Saturday, silence.

teach.h: PALMS TO A CROSS IN FIVE DAYS.
teach.b: People have long noticed how fast it turns, from palms to a cross in five days. Sometimes they say the same crowd that shouted hosanna shouted crucify, but the Gospels don't say who was in either crowd.
Christians keep this week as the center of the whole year.
On Palm Sunday, many churches hand out palm branches and walk in procession, then read the long story of Jesus's death, the Passion, so the whole week is felt at once.

In Russia and other places where palms don't grow, Orthodox Christians carry pussy willow branches instead. In many places, people walk the Stations of the Cross, praying at fourteen scenes along the way to the cross.
And in Jerusalem, pilgrims still walk down the Mount of Olives on Palm Sunday, waving branches, along roughly the road the donkey took.

how: On Palm Sunday many churches bless and hand out palm branches, walk in procession and read the Passion; through Holy Week Christians gather for services each day toward Easter, and many walk the Stations of the Cross.

games.q: you're in the crowd outside Jerusalem. a man on a donkey is coming down the hill, and people around you are cutting branches. what do you do?
o: throw your cloak on the road and shout hosanna.
go into the city before the crowd gets worse.
games.why: the Gospels say the crowd spread cloaks and branches and shouted hosanna. five days later came the cross.

practice: Picture a dusty road down a hill into a crowded city: branches on the ground, the noise, a man on a donkey moving slowly through it all, toward whatever is coming. Walk beside him for a while, and notice what he might be feeling.
If you pray, simply stay with him; if you don't, stay with the picture.

wordCard.voice: Hosanna: a shout that began as a plea, save, please, and became both praise and a prayer for rescue.

orig.note: Greek spelling of Hebrew hoshia na, save, please (Psalm 118:25).

carryVoice: Your line: the week everything turns. Palms first, and then the cross. One hundred fifteen days in.
